q: Which common waterproofing is semi-flexible or rigid and not exposed to weather or sun?
n: Cementitious waterproofing is semi-flexible or rigid. It is used in wet areas and below tiles, not exposed to weather or sun. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; manufacturer data (Sika, BASF).

q: Which waterproofing is a flexible asphalt layer?
n: Bituminous waterproofing is a flexible asphalt-based coating or membrane. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which waterproofing is a single-ply synthetic rubber membrane?
n: EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer) is a single-ply synthetic rubber roofing and waterproofing membrane. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; ASTM D4637.

q: What is the usual liquidated damages rate per day of delay?
n: The usual liquidated damages rate is 1/10 of 1% of the contract price per day of delay. Source: RA 9184 IRR, Sec. 68.

q: When a material is specified by trade name, a substitute needs approval from the:
n: When a material is specified by trade name, any substitute must be approved by the architect-of-record, who judges equivalence. Source: UAP Document 301 (General Conditions); CSI Project Delivery Practice Guide.

q: What is an MSDS?
n: MSDS means Material Safety Data Sheet, giving a product's hazards, safe handling and emergency measures (now SDS under GHS). Source: DOLE OSHS Rule 1090; OSHA Hazard Communication Standard.

q: Which among the following choices is not part of Siteworks?
n: Siteworks cover clearing and grubbing, fences and soil testing. Micro-tunnelled piping is a specialized trenchless utility method under utilities, not general sitework. Source: CSI MasterFormat (Div. 02/31–33).

q: Under the General Requirements, which is not part of the work?
n: General Requirements (Division 1) cover permits, bonds and insurance. Staking (layout) is part of the site work itself. Source: CSI MasterFormat, Division 01.

q: Under what division of the master format specification are Concrete pipes included?
n: Precast concrete pipe is a concrete product, under Division 3 (Concrete, precast concrete) in the 16-division format. Utility piping systems are under Sitework. Source: CSI MasterFormat (1995), Division 3.

q: How many divisions were added to the 16 Division Standard Specifications after 2016?
n: MasterFormat grew from 16 divisions to 50 in the 2004 edition, so 34 divisions were added. The item's "after 2016" refers to its later use locally. Source: CSI MasterFormat 2004 edition.

q: What unit is primarily used in estimating rebar requirements?
n: Rebar is estimated in commercial lengths (6.0, 7.5, 9.0, 10.5, 12.0 m), cut to minimize waste. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate.

q: What goes in Part 1 of the three-part section format?
n: In CSI's three-part section format, Part 1 is General, Part 2 Products and Part 3 Execution. Source: CSI SectionFormat.

q: Which specification names the manufacturer and brand?
n: A closed (proprietary) specification names the manufacturer and brand. Source: CSI Project Delivery Practice Guide.

q: What should be avoided in writing specifications?
n: Specifications should avoid long, ambiguous sentences. Use simple, declarative, itemized statements. Source: CSI Project Delivery Practice Guide (specification language).

q: In construction, what is usually awarded as a sub-contract by the contractor or the client and not part of the general contract?
n: Waterproofing is a specialty trade, usually subcontracted to a specialist applicator for warranty reasons, rather than done by the general contractor. Source: CSI MasterFormat Div. 07; Philippine contracting practice.

q: What standard form sets out the scope of work and contract amount for a construction job?
n: The owner–contractor agreement is the standard contract form setting the scope of work, contract amount and completion time. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 201; AIA A101.

q: Which document defines materials and standards of workmanship?
n: Specifications define the materials, products and standards of workmanship required, complementing the drawings. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 202; CSI MasterFormat.

q: What drawings are submitted to the OBO after construction?
n: After construction, as-built plans are submitted to the OBO with the certificate of completion for the occupancy permit. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 309.

q: What permit must be secured after construction before the owner moves in?
n: A certificate of occupancy must be secured from the Building Official before the building is occupied. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 309.

q: What does the OBO issue once electrical work is substantially complete?
n: When electrical work is complete, the OBO's electrical inspector issues a Certificate of Electrical Inspection, which the utility needs before energizing the service. Source: Philippine Electrical Code; NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III.

q: The invitation to Bid may NOT contain information about __.
n: An invitation to bid names the project, its location and where and when to submit bids. It does not name the deciding party or evaluator. Source: RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act) IRR, Sec. 21; UAP SPP Doc. 204.

q: The instruction to Bidders may NOT contain guidelines on the ___.
n: Instructions to bidders cover bid preparation, submission time, date and place, and mode of delivery. The general description of works is in the invitation and specifications. Source: RA 9184 IRR; UAP SPP Doc. 204.

q: What is the common delay penalty in owner–contractor agreements?
o: 1/10 of 1% of the contract price per day
n: Liquidated damages for delay are commonly 1/10 of 1% of the contract price per calendar day. Source: RA 9184 IRR, Sec. 68; UAP SPP Doc. 201.

q: What does an owner–contractor agreement NOT usually contain?
n: An owner–contractor agreement states the scope, amount and completion time. A waiver and release of liens is a separate document submitted with payments. Source: AIA G706A; UAP SPP Doc. 201.

q: Which section of RA 9266 requires architects to sign and seal their documents?
n: RA 9266 Sec. 20 (Seal, Issuance and Use of Seal) requires architects to sign and seal all architectural plans and documents they prepare. Source: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004), Sec. 20.

q: Who issues the Certificate of Electrical Inspection (CEI)?
n: The Certificate of Electrical Inspection is issued by the city or municipal hall's electrical inspector (OBO), not the utility or contractor. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR; Philippine Electrical Code.

q: Who signs and seals electrical plans with 20 branch circuits?
n: Under RA 7920, electrical plans beyond the master electrician's limited scope (such as 20 branch circuits) must be signed and sealed by a Professional Electrical Engineer. Source: RA 7920 (New Electrical Engineering Law), Sec. 31.

q: Who secures the Certificate of Occupancy?
n: The contractor prepares and signs the certificate of completion and logbook, and in practice processes the certificate of occupancy for the owner/permittee, who files it. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 309.

q: How many days before the release of the building permit?
n: The Building Official must act on a complete building permit application within 15 days of payment. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 304; NBC IRR Rule III.

q: In which phase does the architect produce a complete set of drawings and help the owner with bidding?
n: In the contract documents phase the architect prepares the complete working drawings and specifications and helps the owner with bidding. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 202, Regular Design Services.

q: What does the Building Official issue to let the owner proceed with construction?
n: The Building Official issues the building permit, which allows the owner to begin construction. Source: PD 1096, Sec. 301.

q: Issued by the Building Official for accessory parts of the project with very special functions or use which are indicated in the plans and specifications that accompany the building permit application.
n: An accessory permit is issued by the Building Official for accessory parts of a project with very special functions or uses, as shown in the permit plans. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: Which permits cover excavation, foundation encroachment, fences up to 1.80 m, sidewalks, scaffolding, signs and demolition?
n: Accessory permits cover minor works: excavation, foundation encroachment, fences up to 1.80 m, sidewalks, scaffolding, signs and demolition. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: What must the owner provide for a building permit?
o: TCT, real property tax receipt and tax declaration
n: To show ownership for a building permit, the owner submits the TCT, the current real property tax receipt and the tax declaration. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302.

q: Needed document in processing Occupancy Permit.
n: For an occupancy permit the owner submits the construction logbook, signed and sealed, with the certificate of completion and as-built plans. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 309.

q: Instructions that supplement or modify drawings, specs, & general conditions of the contract.
n: Special provisions (supplementary conditions) supplement or modify the drawings, specifications and general conditions for a particular project. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 201; AIA A201 Supplementary Conditions.
